reviewer_scope: IO area-owner independent source review of six device-only fixture/probe corrections authored by UI owner under root GO.
source_verdict: No concrete source blocker found to the lead-scheduled focused IO native-descriptor and parser diagnostic; this is not a runtime or whole-suite approval.
positive_source_checks: IO reference construction is private and the used factories reject non-REG/FIFO and zero identities; each local actual known descriptor must have the same native st_ino and fdinfo ino. File path stat is additionally compared to the opened descriptor.

IO actual FileProvider native source descriptor is REG-calibrated before transfer. The real error pipe is FIFO-calibrated; actual mode and fdinfo identity accompany the existing stat device/inode in its provider Bundle. Validation failures close owned descriptors and retain suppressed close errors.

Picker DocumentsProvider REG-calibrates its actual opened descriptor before transfer. Its base FileProvider reference calibrates a real received read-only descriptor and closes that extra handle before invoking the production operation.

Both probes snapshot only this process numeric FD names, acquire an owned duplicate, strictly read its inode header, and exclude only a different unsigned inode before native stat. A same-inode candidate still requires fstat device/inode equality; no failed stat is converted to zero.

Header parse rejects missing/duplicate/empty/signed/nondecimal/internal-whitespace/overflow values. Unsigned64 maximum is represented without numeric truncation; unsigned-to-signed conversion of reference bits round-trips through native signed Long. Valid unrelated zero is distinct from a forbidden zero target.

Only IOException wrapping EBADF at initial duplication is tolerated. Header read/parse, duplicate close and all same-inode fstat errors propagate. Metadata readers and duplicate handles are use-owned.

Native IO control keeps two distinct real files open, unlinks one while open, demands exact1 counts and unchanged offsets repeatedly, then demands zero after close. Real pipe endpoints retain2-to1-to0 checks. Picker control requires an intentionally open file to fail the zero-count assertion with the expected diagnostic and detects a distinct unlinked open file.
Native hardlink method still calls real Os.link and contains no exclusion/skip/security change. All production sources and existing host/iOS/browser tests remain outside this correction.
limits_not_hidden_by_verdict: Focused selection exercises the IO native probe and IO parser only, not picker helper compilation/execution, real provider calibration, read-error pipe IPC or public Activity/save operations.

Parser streams the complete fdinfo line sequence rather than a fixed bounded header. It does not store or log the full content, but malformed overlong-line and reader-error policy controls were not added. Kernel-generated controlled proc data limits the present scope; no general hostile-input bound is certified.

Regular-file controls use two distinct file identities, not two simultaneous descriptors sharing one regular-file identity. The same-identity2-to1-to0 control currently covers a real pipe. A same-file dup count/offset control remains useful.

Received FileProvider descriptor gets its own fdinfo/fstat calibration, but this helper does not independently compare its device/inode against the caller path reference. Actual retained-source integration must still show a nonzero matching count; this focused run cannot prove all cross-process identity relationships.

Per-reference fdinfo/stat agreement is verified for these task-owned REG/FIFO fixtures, not arbitrary overlay/FUSE/custom-getattr filesystems. Raw mount IDs are deliberately not used as a negative filter.
No actual inaccessible-fdinfo or same-inode protected-collision negative device scenario has executed. Static propagation is not substituted for those boundary tests.
Root source-hash/focused runtime results must be finalized before any pass claim. All earlier complete method failures, including native hardlink denial, remain preserved.
